title: A Global Convergence of Multidimensional Poverty and Climate Hazards: Insights from 2025 MPI Report

detail.title: A Global Convergence of Multidimensional Poverty and Climate Hazards: Insights from 2025 MPI Report

publicationDetails.detailsText: A smaller version of this paper is published in Policy Circle

detail.abstract:
The 2025 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report presents evidence of convergence between poverty and climate hazards. Among 1.1 billion people living in acute multidimensional poverty, approximately 887 million live in subnational locations exposed to at least one climate hazards (high heat, drought, floods, or air pollution). Of these, 608 million of poor people are subjected to excessive heat, 577 million to air pollution, 465 million to floods and 207 million to drought. Across the ten MPI deprivations considered, global poor population is particularly exposed to specific deprivations; 970 million do not have clean cooking fuel; 878 million lack adequate housing; 830 million lack sanitation; 635 million are undernourished; and hundreds of millions face severe educational deprivations. State of deprivation is notably high among children and rural populations, and in regions such as South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa, as well as in middle-income countries.

The subnational analysis for India shows dramatic variation compared with the national multidimensional poverty incidence of 16.4%: Kerala has the lowest rate (0.86%) while Bihar has the highest (34.7%). Poverty in India is rural-centric: 90% of the poor reside in rural areas, which account for 69% of the population. About 69% of India’s poor are concentrated in six states — Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal — with deprivations in cooking fuel, housing, and sanitation being the most prevalent. These results highlight how climate risks exacerbate development challenges and increase regional and population subgroup inequalities, undermining recent poverty-reduction gains. Context-specific interventions are urgently required, specifically that addresses deprivations and reduce climate exposure, and safeguard achievements and guide future policy.

title: Robust Quantum-Compatible Causal Inference under MNAR

detail.title: Robust Quantum-Compatible Causal Inference under MNAR
detail.abstract: We propose a novel estimator inspired by quantum causal inference, where causal structure emerges through observation. Unlike classical frameworks with fixed graphs, our approach treats measurement as a source of causal directionality, requiring bidirectional and observer-aware inference. To address high-dimensional, low-sample-size challenges, we reinterpret Missing Not At Random as a proxy for observer-induced perturbation. Our MNAR-aware doubly robust estimator integrates variational autoencoders for latent representation, selection-aware reweighting, and penalized empirical likelihood to induce sparsity. We further incorporate covariate balancing propensity scores and robust techniques to mitigate outlier effects. Extensive simulations and biomedical evaluations demonstrate superior performance over existing methods, validating MNAR as a structural signal rather than a nuisance.

title: Robust Quantum Inference: Latent Variable Modeling for MNAR, Noise Mitigation, and Quantum Causality

detail.title: Robust Quantum Inference: Latent Variable Modeling for MNAR, Noise Mitigation, and Quantum Causality
detail.abstract: We propose a unified Penalized Empirical Likelihood (PEL) framework for quantum inference that rigorously integrates temporal dynamics, spatial correlations, and Missing Not At Random (MNAR) mechanisms. While the broader architecture supports bidirectional inference to uncover latent quantum features, this study focuses primarily on mitigating the intrinsic contamination of raw quantum data-stemming from gate errors and decoherence. We introduce a novel noise-suppression strategy that substitutes error-prone observations.. By encoding physical constraints such as Complete Positivity and Trace Preservation (CPTP) as estimating equations, our framework ensures parsimony and physical realizability. Extensive simulations and real-world validation on IBM Quantum processors and 8-photon tomography datasets demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms classical baselines in predictive accuracy, offering a scalable solution for characterizing Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) systems.

title: Persistence in the Mint Stock Markets: Evidence from a Fractional Integration Model
affiliations: Brunel University London - Department of Economics and Finance, University of Navarra - Department of Economics,  and Federal University of Technology Akure (FUTA)

detail.title: Persistence in the Mint Stock Markets: Evidence from a Fractional Integration Model

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper investigates persistence in the MINT (Mexico, Indonesia, Nigeria, Turkey) stock markets applying fractional integration methods to daily data from 1 January 2022 to 31 October 2025. Different model specifications are estimated for prices, log prices and log returns under the assumption of white noise and autocorrelated errors respectively. Mean reversion is found in most cases for prices with autocorrelated errors, which implies that shocks have only temporary effects in this case. Turkey displays the lowest degrees of integration, while Nigeria has the highest for both prices and log-prices. Structural breaks are found in the case of stock prices in all countries, with market inefficiencies appearing to be present in the most recent period characterized by geopolitical uncertainty resulting from the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

title: Climate Policy Credibility, Learning Dynamics, and Institutional Quality in Critical Mineral Value Chains

detail.title: Climate Policy Credibility, Learning Dynamics, and Institutional Quality in Critical Mineral Value Chains
detail.abstract: Should resource exporters delay climate action to preserve competitiveness? We develop a dynamic general equilibrium model of critical-mineral value chains in which governments choose multi-instrument transition packages subject to family-specific credibility constraints. Calibrated to Chile, Australia, and Indonesia, early implementation (2025 rather than 2035) raises welfare and reduces cumulative upstream emissions in annual equilibrium simulations. Welfare gains are sizable for Chile (5.6% of GDP) and Indonesia (13.0%) in the baseline calibration, while Australia is a more marginal case whose welfare effect is sensitive to trade parameters. A welfare decomposition shows that market surplus dominates the gains in Chile/Australia, whereas avoided emissions damages dominate in Indonesia due to high emissions intensity. Credibility constraints bind heterogeneously across standards/charges, tariffs, and subsidies, implying that institutional quality shapes both the feasible composition of transition packages and the incentives for innovation and abatement.

title: The Physics of Economics: A Novel Framework for Sustainable, Equitable, Post-Scarcity Economics

detail.title: The Physics of Economics: A Novel Framework for Sustainable, Equitable, Post-Scarcity Economics
detail.abstract: For three centuries, economic orthodoxy has operated on the assumption that money must be created as debt to facilitate growth, creating a systemic imperative for exponential expansion that now conflicts with planetary thermodynamic limits. This paper proposes a novel framework, the Modern Economic Theory & System Implementation Roadmap (METSIR), which grounds monetary policy in physical laws rather than debt obligations. We introduce the Lumen, a sovereign currency pegged to thermodynamic energy capacity (measured in J/s), and Non-Tradable Credits (NTC), a parallel instrument for valuing nonmarket labor. By decoupling currency creation from debt, the framework eliminates the mathematical inevitability of financial crises and transforms deflation from a recessionary threat into a "Deflationary Dividend"-a mechanism where systemic efficiency gains accrue directly to currency holders as purchasing power. We present mathematical proofs demonstrating that this energy-pegged model achieves general equilibrium with zero inflation, neutralizes speculative bubbles through algorithmic leverage constraints, and creates a stable pathway to a post-scarcity civilization. Complete system architecture is provided, including currency specification, the dualcurrency system, asset tokenization for capital formation without debt, performancebased capital access, price discovery mechanisms, and the Genesis Transaction for converting legacy debt to asset-backed instruments. Implementation requires sortitionbased governance with conviction voting and automatic recall to prevent oligarchy. The framework is universal in principle but particular in application, designed to be adapted by nations and communities to their unique contexts.

title: Minimum Energy Performance Standards and House Price Capitalization: Evidence from France’s Rental Ban on “Energy Sieves”
affiliations: Audencia Business School and Audencia Business School

detail.title: Minimum Energy Performance Standards and House Price Capitalization: Evidence from France’s Rental Ban on “Energy Sieves”
detail.abstract: Energy performance disclosure is increasingly paired with minimum energy performance standards to accelerate the capitalization of energy inefficiency into housing prices and strengthen homeowners’ incentives to renovate inefficient dwellings. We study the 2021 French policy implementing a progressive rental ban on the least energy-efficient dwellings (“energy sieves”) and examine whether it has affected house prices. Using more than 900,000 housing transactions over 2014–2024, we document that energy sieves sell at an additional discount of about 5 percentage points following the policy announcement. For owners of rented energy sieves, this discount helps reduce the gap between expected renovation costs to achieve compliance and expected sale loss due to non-compliance. Consistent with renovation costs driving the post-ban announcement discount, the latter is much larger for houses that are costlier to renovate. The increase in the supply of G-rated houses in the sales market is also concentrated among those that are costlier to renovate.

title: Agroecological Practices Reflect Existing Inequalities Among Zimbabwean Farmers, Rather Than Transform Them
affiliations: Centre De Coopération Internationale En Recherche Agronomique Pour Le Développement (CIRAD), Université Montpellier I, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University and Centre De Coopération Internationale En Recherche Agronomique Pour Le Développement (CIRAD)

detail.title: Agroecological Practices Reflect Existing Inequalities Among Zimbabwean Farmers, Rather Than Transform Them
detail.abstract: CONTEXTImproved crop and livestock management practices could contribute to solving food insecurity and poverty among smallholder farmers in Zimbabwe. Agroecological practices, which rely on the use and recycling of local resources to reduce dependency on costly external inputs, are increasingly being claimed as suitable options for resource-constrained farmers.OBJECTIVEThe objective of this study was to assess how adoption of improved crop and livestock practices, including agroecological ones, varied among different farm types. We hypothesised that agroecological practices would be preferentially adopted by lower-resource endowed farm types.METHODSData from a household survey of 605 farms across a representative sub-humid district and a representative semi-arid district in Zimbabwe, documenting adoption of 32 improved crop and livestock practices, 14 of which classified as agroecological, were used for this study. A farm typology based on practice adoption was delineated using Multiple Correspondence Analysis, after which the socio-economic characteristics of the farm types and their associations with farm performance were assessed.RESULTS and CONCLUSIONSOur analysis revealed that farmers adopting a broader range of improved practices – including agroecological ones – were generally the wealthier and more resource-endowed households. Importantly, we found that these same farms were also more diverse in crop and livestock species, indicating that farm diversity was positively associated with wealth, resource access, and production capacity rather than being a compensatory strategy of poorer households. Disappointingly, we observed limited associations between the adoption of improved practices and production or diet outcomes.SIGNIFICANCEThe study points to the need for targeted support to less-endowed households, addressing not only technical but also socio-economic and institutional constraints to both diversification and improved practice adoption.

title: Research Paper: The Application of the IPPO Model in Organizational Recruitment and Talent Management

detail.title: Research Paper: The Application of the IPPO Model in Organizational Recruitment and Talent Management
detail.abstract:
Background: Traditional organizational recruitment and human resource management often prioritize technical competencies (skills) and behavioral traits (personality) while overlooking the most profound driver of human performance: an individual’s internal life philosophy. When a discrepancy exists between an employee’s core beliefs and the organization’s cultural values, the result is often "philosophical friction," leading to professional burnout, high turnover rates, and systemic inefficiency.

Objective: This paper explores the application of the IPPO Model (Interest, Personality, Philosophy, and Outcome)—developed by S. Ahmed—as a strategic tool for organizational recruitment. The study aims to demonstrate how measuring "purpose-based consistency" can create a more stable, humane, and high-performing workforce.

Methodology: The research utilizes the IPPO framework to categorize recruitment needs into a three-tier managerial impact model: Ground Influencers (Lower Management), Cultural Translators (Middle Management), and Philosophy Cascades (Senior Leadership). It examines how a candidate’s internal compass (Philosophy) dictates their decision-making style and interpersonal dynamics within these tiers.

Results: The application of the model reveals that long-term employee stability and performance are highest when "High Alignment" is achieved between the individual’s philosophy and the company’s mission. The paper identifies that leadership failures are frequently rooted in philosophical misalignments—such as a "self-centered" life philosophy operating within a "service-oriented" organizational structure.

Conclusion: The IPPO model provides a comprehensive roadmap for modern HR departments to transition from efficiency-based hiring to alignment-based talent acquisition. By integrating philosophical mapping into the recruitment process, organizations can foster a culture of transparency, minimize mental fatigue among staff, and ensure that leadership at all levels reinforces a consistent ethical and operational vision.

title: Financial Networks Under the Lens of Quantum Entanglement: A New Framework for Systemic Risk
affiliations: , UCL Institute of Finance and Technology ,  and

detail.title: Financial Networks Under the Lens of Quantum Entanglement: A New Framework for Systemic Risk
detail.abstract: We develop a framework for systemic risk modelling that embeds finite state continuous time Markov chain (CTMC) models of bank health into a quantum density matrix representation. In the classical benchmark each bank has a latent health state following a CTMC, and three lenses, solvency (R), liquidity (L) and market valuation (M), are noisy, conditionally independent signals of this single latent factor. In the quantum extension each bank is represented by a density matrix that evolves under a Lindblad generator. The solvency lens R is a projective measurement in a fixed basis, while the liquidity and market lenses are projective measurements in rotated bases that may not commute with R. We embed any CTMC generator into a Lindblad generator so that, with only commuting lenses, the quantum model is observationally equivalent to the classical benchmark and coherence has no economic effect. With at least one noncommuting lens, and especially with entanglement, there exist joint distributions over multi lens, multi bank stress indicators that no comparable single factor CTMC can generate. On the same data the quantum model attains a lower negative log likelihood than fitted classical independent and single factor baselines. We illustrate this with Bell and GHZ style examples and finance styled synthetic data mapping CDS spreads, liquidity spreads and equity returns into R, L and M stress probabilities. Classical models then misestimate systemic event probabilities such as the chance that all core banks are simultaneously stressed, while the quantum latent health model improves fit.

title: Salience Theory and Risk Anomalies
affiliations: Birmingham Business School and University of Hull

detail.title: Salience Theory and Risk Anomalies
detail.abstract: Investor demand for stocks is driven by their salient returns (Bordalo, Gennaioli, and Shleifer, 2012). We hypothesize that high-risk stocks are more likely to yield salient returns than low-risk stocks. Using various risk measures, we show that the risk-return relation is significantly positive for stocks with salient downsides but negative for stocks with salient upsides. We provide evidence that retail investors pay strong attention to salient stock payoffs and demand more (less) high-risk stocks in the presence of salient upsides (downsides). Our findings hold after controlling for alternative explanations including lottery preference, arbitrage risk, reference-dependent preference, disagreement and coskewness risk.

title: Total Solar Irradiance: Evidence from a Long-Memory Model
affiliations: Brunel University London - Department of Economics and Finance, University of Navarra - Department of Economics and Universidad Francisco de Vitoria

detail.title: Total Solar Irradiance: Evidence from a Long-Memory Model

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper analyses aggregated data (5 days period) on total solar irradiance (TSI) based on the 3D MHD numerical simulations of solar surface and atmosphere (Yeo et al., 2017), from 30 April 2010 to 8 July 2023. It improves upon earlier studies by including in the sample the most recent satellite observations and by applying fractional integration methods. These are more general than alternative ones and the most suitable to obtain evidence on the stochastic properties of the series, such as its degree of persistence, and the transitory or permanent effects of shocks. The results indicate that TSI is characterised by long-range dependence or long-memory behaviour, with an order of integration higher than 0 and smaller than 1 and evidence of non-linearities; thus, the effects of shocks are long-lived. Further, the recursive analysis indicates a changing pattern across the sample period. In terms of climate change, the key issue remains the balance between incoming solar radiation and outgoing thermal radiation.

title: Why Educational Development Matters: The Long-Term Impact of Ancient Chinese Shuyuan on Intergenerational Upward Educational Mobility
affiliations: Anhui University, Wuhan University - School of Economics and Management, Guangdong University of Foreign Studies and

detail.title: Why Educational Development Matters: The Long-Term Impact of Ancient Chinese Shuyuan on Intergenerational Upward Educational Mobility
detail.abstract: The Shuyuan was a significant educational institution in China from the Tang to the Qing dynasties, developing unique educational and cultural characteristics over its millennium-long evolution. Leveraging city-level variations in the establishment of Shuyuan during the Ming and Qing periods, this paper identifies a long-term positive causal effect of these educational institutions on the intergenerational accumulation of human capital in contemporary China. The study finds that a 1% increase in the number of Shuyuan during the Ming and Qing dynasties is associated with an approximate 0.08% rise in the rate of intergenerational upward educational mobility and a 0.06% increase in average years of schooling. The long-term human capital accumulation effect of academy construction can be explained through multiple channels, including the cultural inheritance of valuing education, social capital, as well as modern educational facilities and education quality. This research provides new empirical evidence on the long-term significance of educational institutions in economic development.

title: The Great Loop -Assessing Systemic Financial Fragility in the AI-Centric Economy

detail.title: The Great Loop -Assessing Systemic Financial Fragility in the AI-Centric Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Disclaimer: The views and opinions expressed herein are solely my own. They do not represent, reflect, or imply endorsement by any organization, institution, or employer with which I am currently or have previously been affiliated. The data has been verified to be correct at the time of writing it.

keywords: Network Contagion Risks AI Bubble -Is it real?

detail.abstract: AI is transforming the real economy, yet the financial system built around it is increasingly fragile. This paper maps the “Great Loop”, which is a reflexive cycle in which hyperscalers, chipmakers, and AI labs reinforce each other’s valuations through equity stakes, cloud contracts, and GPU commitments. I benchmark this structure against six historical bubble indicators, and analyse current market conditions, including elevated P/E ratios and index concentration data as of Dec'25. Using a network contagion model, I review how shocks could propagate across this ecosystem, and how the concentrated exposures and circular capital flows can magnify losses tcreating systemic vulnerabilities.  While AI matches five of six bubble parameters, the strong underlying technological fundamentals and real assets of the companies provide partial insulation. The paper offers a framework for understanding these dynamics and outlines buffers, risks, and investment considerations for the next phase of AI‑driven growth.

title: The IPPO Model: A Philosophical Approach to Person-Organization Fit in Recruitment and Talent Management

detail.title: The IPPO Model: A Philosophical Approach to Person-Organization Fit in Recruitment and Talent Management
detail.abstract: The enduring challenge in Human Resource Management (HRM) is achieving optimal Person-Organization (P-O) Fit and Person-Job (P-J) Fit, which are critical predictors of job satisfaction, performance, and retention. Traditional assessment methods, while effective in measuring skills and personality traits, often overlook the deepest layer of human motivation: the individual's core philosophy of life. This paper introduces the IPPO Model (Interest + Personality + Philosophy = Outcomes) as a novel, comprehensive framework to enhance the precision of P-O and P-J fit assessments. The model integrates three distinct psychological layers-Interest (vocational preference), Personality (stable behavioral traits, e.g., Big Five), and Philosophy (core beliefs and values)-to predict long-term professional Outcomes such as engagement and tenure. By operationalizing Philosophy as a measurable component of fit, the IPPO model enables organizations to move beyond mere competency matching to achieve a profound alignment of purpose and values. This paper details the IPPO framework, reviews its theoretical foundations in organizational behavior, and provides a practical analysis of its application in philosophical recruitment, talent development, and the creation of a purposebased organizational culture.

title: Black-Scholes with Impulse Forcing: A PDE Framework with Dirac Delta Forcing

detail.title: Black-Scholes with Impulse Forcing: A PDE Framework with Dirac Delta Forcing
detail.abstract: This paper develops a framework for pricing derivatives around scheduled market events by introducing Dirac delta distributions as forcing terms in the Black-Scholes partial differential equation. Unlike jump-diffusion models which modify the underlying stochastic process, the approach I develop treats discrete-time events: earnings announcements, central bank decisions, or flash crashes, as external impulses acting on the pricing PDE at known times. The central result is an equivalence theorem: Dirac forcing is mathematically equivalent to imposing jump conditions on the option value surface. This reduces the measure-driven problem to a sequence of classical parabolic equations. I derive explicit Green's function representations showing that shocks propagate via convolution with the fundamental solution, prove that Greek discontinuities are determined by derivatives of the shock amplitude (∆∆ = α ′ , ∆Γ = α ′′), and introduce economically motivated shock specifications with market interpretations. The framework provides analytical tractability for event-driven pricing while maintaining consistency with no-arbitrage principles.

title: Mandatory Human-Machine Employment Ratios: A Compute-Based Framework for Labor Protection in the Age of Automation

detail.title: Mandatory Human-Machine Employment Ratios: A Compute-Based Framework for Labor Protection in the Age of Automation
detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence and robotics increasingly displace human labor, existing policy responses-primarily robot taxation proposals-face fundamental challenges in definition, measurement, and enforcement. This paper introduces a novel regulatory mechanism: mandatory human-machine employment ratios indexed to verifiable proxies of automation intensity, specifically industrial electricity consumption and computational capacity (measured in FLOPS). We propose a formula-based approach where minimum human employment levels (Nmin) are calculated as a function of three measurable inputs: electricity consumption (Pe), compute scale (Ca), and robotic equipment count (Ra), with industry-specific adjustment coefficients. Firms failing to meet the computed employment floor must either hire additional workers or pay a Social Contribution Fund penalty with progressive rates. Unlike robot taxes, which struggle with definitional ambiguity and create perverse incentives to offshore automation, our approach leverages existing metering infrastructure (power grids, customs data, tax records) for cross-validation, making evasion significantly more difficult. We present detailed parameter estimates for seven industry categories, enforcement mechanisms utilizing multi-source data fusion, and a five-year phased implementation roadmap.

title: Political Instability and Foreign Direct Investment in Nigeria: Evidence, Channels, and Development Implications

detail.title: Political Instability and Foreign Direct Investment in Nigeria: Evidence, Channels, and Development Implications
detail.abstract: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is a critical driver of economic growth, technology transfer, and structural transformation in developing economies. Despite Nigeria's large market size and abundant natural resources, FDI inflows into the country have remained volatile and below potential. This paper examines the role of political instability in shaping FDI inflows to Nigeria. Drawing on empirical evidence from existing literature and country-level trends, the study identifies key channels through which political instability, such as policy uncertainty, weak institutions, corruption, and security challenges, affects foreign investors' decisions. The findings suggest that persistent political instability discourages long-term and productivity-enhancing investments, thereby constraining economic diversification and sustainable development. The paper concludes with policy implications emphasizing institutional strengthening, political stability, and governance reforms as prerequisites for attracting sustainable FDI.

title: The Spillovers of LSAPs on Banks in the Euro Area
affiliations: University of Basel - Center for Economic Science,  and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: The Spillovers of LSAPs on Banks in the Euro Area

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the spillovers of large-scale asset purchases (LSAPs) in the U.S. on financial intermediation in the euro area using bank-level supervisory data and high-frequency identified policy surprises. Our detailed panel data permit us to trace the impact of LSAPs through bank balance sheets. We find that the Federal Reserve affects credit provision in the euro area through a channel that we refer to as the "international bank capital channel" of unconventional monetary policy. In response to an LSAP shock that leads to a steepening of the U.S. Treasury yield curve, the Treasury positions of euro area banks shrink, capital ratios worsen, and banks that are less well capitalized contract their lending relative to banks that are better capitalized. Our results are consistent with an important role of revaluation effects, imperfect risk hedging, and credit as an adjustment margin for banks in the proximity of regulatory capital constraints.

title: Investment Mobilization as Infrastructure: Introducing the Investment Mobilization Management System (IMMS)

detail.title: Investment Mobilization as Infrastructure: Introducing the Investment Mobilization Management System (IMMS)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or identifiable personal information. As a conceptual and analytical working paper based on publicly available sources, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Despite decades of policy reform, project preparation facilities, and investment promotion efforts, many African and emerging-market economies continue to struggle with the consistent conversion of investment opportunities into bankable, capital-deployable outcomes. While capital availability is often cited as the primary constraint, this paper argues that the more fundamental challenge lies in the absence of a coherent system for investment mobilisation, one that aligns policy intent, project readiness, capital compatibility, and execution governance across public and private actors. This paper introduces the concept of the Investment Mobilization Management System (IMMS) as a missing infrastructure layer in contemporary development finance and investment governance. Drawing on cross-sectoral evidence from public-sector investment pipelines, private capital deployment practices, and development finance interventions, the paper conceptualizes investment mobilization as a systemic coordination problem rather than a transactional or informational deficit. It argues that treating mobilization as infrastructure, rather than as episodic deal-making, creates the conditions for standardization, continuity, and trust across complex public-private ecosystems.

title: Destroy and Build? Economic Effects of Centres de Regroupement in the Algerian War

detail.title: Destroy and Build? Economic Effects of Centres de Regroupement in the Algerian War
detail.abstract: Urbanization is generally accompanied by development. However, whether abrupt unintended urbanization can stimulate future progress is an open question. The French government constructed thousands of Centres de Regroupement (resettlement centers) in Algeria during the Independence War, to which the army forcefully relocated around 2.5 million civilians. The policy took these civilians away from their previous agricultural lives, and concentrated them within prison camps. Using the heterogeneity in treatment across regions, Difference-inDifferences estimates show that the policy has a persistent negative impact on the population growth overall but a continuing positive impact on urbanization. To address the endogeneity, I use the facts that i) the army implemented the policy out of purely military concerns and ii) the whole process lacked coherent planning from the authority. The findings provide novel insights into the long-run economic impacts of unintended urbanization.

title: Stablecoins: A Law and Economics Analysis

detail.title: Stablecoins: A Law and Economics Analysis
detail.abstract: Stablecoins have emerged as a central innovation within the crypto-financial ecosystem, aiming to mitigate the price volatility of unbacked cryptocurrencies while raising new concerns for financial stability, monetary policy, and regulatory oversight. Positioned at the intersection of financial innovation and legal uncertainty, their rapid adoption challenges the architecture of modern monetary systems. This study analyzes the evolving role of stablecoins through an interdisciplinary law and economics approach. It examines the functioning of different stablecoin models, the systemic risks revealed by recent market events, including the collapse of TerraUSD, the failure of centralized crypto platforms, and the banking turmoil involving Silvergate Bank, Signature Bank, and Silicon Valley Bank, and the regulatory responses emerging across jurisdictions. The analysis focuses on the regulatory frameworks adopted in the European Union and the United States, with particular attention to the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) Regulation, recent U.S. legislative initiatives such as the Genius Act and the Wyoming Stable Token Act, and their implications for reserve backing, governance, and supervisory oversight. The paper further investigates the interaction between private digital money and sovereign digital initiatives, including central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and the European project for a Digital Euro, assessing potential complementarities, competitive dynamics, and integration scenarios. The central argument advanced is that stablecoins, if subject to robust legal and prudential safeguards, may function as complementary instruments to sovereign currencies within digital payment infrastructures rather than as substitutes. However, fragmented regulation, insufficient transparency, and growing financial interconnectedness continue to amplify systemic vulnerabilities. The paper concludes by advocating a balanced and forward looking regulatory framework capable of preserving innovation while safeguarding financial stability and the integrity of monetary systems.

title: The Macroeconomic Impact of Fiscal Policies Reflecting State Dependency : The Case of Korea

detail.title: The Macroeconomic Impact of Fiscal Policies Reflecting State Dependency : The Case of Korea

keywords: Economic Stabilization JEL Classification: C32 E32 E62 H50

detail.abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Korea's fiscal policy for economic stabilization, focusing on state dependency. Using the Auerbach and Gorodnichenko (2013)'s model, the analysis addresses short-term government expenditure data by components and identifies forecast errors to capture unexpected expenditure changes. Results show that fiscal policy is more effective in slack, with a higher multiplier effect in slack than in boom. Unexpected government expenditure shocks are more impactful than anticipated changes. Among components, government investment expenditure yields the highest multiplier effect, with direct government purchases proving the most effective, surpassing unity in impact compared to other types of expenditure.

title: Building Shared Horizons: Fostering a Sustainable Environment Through India-China Renewable Energy Cooperation

detail.title: Building Shared Horizons: Fostering a Sustainable Environment Through India-China Renewable Energy Cooperation
detail.abstract: Climate change driven by rising greenhouse gas emissions is one of the most serious challenges to the global community. In recent years, this trajectory has begun to change. Both nations are increasingly repositioning themselves from major contributors to climate stress toward prominent actors in the global renewable energy transition. By investing heavily in large scale clean energy projects and nurturing robust domestic renewable markets, India and China are steadily emerging as central forces in the pursuit of environmental sustainability. This article examines the present state of renewable energy development in China and India and explores the areas where cooperation between the two countries could be most effective. It considers how shared efforts may help speed up the adoption of renewable energy not only within their borders but across the wider South Asian region. Using recent data and policy trends as its foundation, the work highlights the role of joint initiatives in areas such as technology sharing and sustainability. It further offers practical policy insights and strategic recommendations aimed at strengthening future collaborative efforts and advancing regional energy security and climate goals.

title: Mapping Effects of Road Accidents on the Public Pension System Research
affiliations: University of the Basque Country, University of the Basque Country and University of the Basque Country

detail.title: Mapping Effects of Road Accidents on the Public Pension System Research
detail.abstract: Road traffic accidents generate innumerable costs for those affected and for the public health and pension systems. Although there is extensive academic literature analysing the consequences on health and the health system, there is less academic tradition regarding the study of the effects on public pension systems.,This study presents a bibliometric and science-mapping analysis of research on the economic losses resulting from road traffic accidents. Using Scopus and Web of Science (combined dataset; 1974–2024), we classify the literature by topic, methods and data; map thematic clusters and their evolution; and identify under-studied areas — notably the direct and indirect effects on public pension systems. Our analysis yields four principal clusters and shows a small but growing interest in pension-related valuations and actuarial treatment of traffic injuries.,The main results of the co-word analysis and in-depth review of the most relevant papers reveal four main thematic groups or clusters in the field, headed by the keywords: Humans, Road, Cost-of-Illness and Hospitalisation, which provide a holistic view of the broad and multidisciplinary field of research.,The authors conclude by noting the growing—although still relatively scarce—interest in this topic among the scientific community, the shift of interest from more developed countries to emerging ones, and the need to bridge the gap between the academic weight and the economic and social relevance linked to this issue.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Sustainable Investment: Modeling ESG
affiliations: Ibn Tofail University, Ibn Tofail University and Ibn Tofail University

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Sustainable Investment: Modeling ESG
detail.abstract: This study examines the determinants of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance among Moroccan listed firms by integrating traditional financial indicators with alternative data sources using artificial intelligence methods. Based on a panel dataset covering the 2014–2018 period, the analysis combines a Generalized Least Squares (GLS) econometric model with a Random Forest algorithm to assess both explanatory and predictive dimensions. Results indicate that profitability (ROA), firm size, and governance quality exert a positive and significant influence on ESG scores, while leverage negatively affects sustainability performance. Liquidity also contributes positively but to a lesser extent. The Random Forest model demonstrates strong predictive power (R2 = 0.876 in cross-validation), confirming the robustness of AI-based modeling for ESG assessment. Feature importance analysis reveals governance and profitability as the primary determinants of ESG outcomes, followed by firm size and leverage structure. Moreover, the inclusion of alternative data derived from media, open data platforms, and social networks significantly improves model accuracy (adjusted R2 +0.088; p < 0.01), underscoring the added value of non-financial information in sustainability evaluation. These findings highlight the potential of artificial intelligence to enhance the precision, transparency, and reliability of ESG measurement in emerging markets. The study contributes to bridging the gap between data science and sustainable finance, offering actionable insights for investors, regulators, and firms seeking to integrate ESG criteria into strategic decision-making.

title: Foreign Investment, Inequality, and the Kuznets Curve: A Sectoral and Historical Analysis of FDI in Francophone Africa (1990-2022)

detail.title: Foreign Investment, Inequality, and the Kuznets Curve: A Sectoral and Historical Analysis of FDI in Francophone Africa (1990-2022)
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between foreign direct investment (FDI) and income inequality in 21 former French colonies in Sub-Saharan Africa from 1990 to 2022 using fixed-effects panel regressions. It hypothesizes that FDI follows a Kuznets-style inverted U-curve: initially increasing inequality but later reducing it at higher levels of investment when institutional conditions improve. Further examination of this hypothesis will be done through a sectoral analysis. Particular focus will be put on French-origin FDI to question the deeper neo-colonial economic dependencies that may be associated with such aid. Taken together, these findings suggest that FDI can support equitable development, but only when carefully aligned with domestic policy capacity, institutional strength, and strategic sectoral planning.

title: Causal Analysis of Barriers to Women’s Cooperative Financial Inclusion in Africa: A Delphi–Fuzzy DEMATEL Approach
affiliations: Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University and Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University

detail.title: Causal Analysis of Barriers to Women’s Cooperative Financial Inclusion in Africa: A Delphi–Fuzzy DEMATEL Approach
detail.abstract: Despite sustained inclusion policies, women remain financially excluded from cooperative systems in low-income African contexts. This study develops a causal, uncertainty-sensitive framework to identify and prioritise the systemic barriers underlying this exclusion. The framework integrates a Fuzzy Delphi process with the Fuzzy DEMATEL method, drawing on evaluations from 12 experts across 20 identified barriers to model causal and interdependent exclusion dynamics under uncertainty. Drawing on evaluations from twelve domain experts, the analysis reveals a hierarchical exclusion structure in which lack of formal identification, irregular income, and limited collateral or asset ownership emerge as dominant causal drivers that trigger cascading effects across socio-cultural, institutional, and digital domains. In opposite, constraints frequently targeted by policy interventions, such as limited financial literacy, digital exclusion, high transaction costs, and weak representation in cooperative governance, are shown to function primarily as downstream effects rather than root causes. Robustness tests confirm the stability of the causal structure. By shifting the analytical focus from isolated determinants to systemic causality, this study advances the literature on gendered financial exclusion and provides evidence-based guidance for prioritising high-leverage structural interventions to enhance women’s financial inclusion in cooperative systems.

title: The Hope for Africa, through Regulation, Infrastructure, and Skills
affiliations: and Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK)

detail.title: The Hope for Africa, through Regulation, Infrastructure, and Skills
detail.abstract: This study examines the phenomenon of entrepreneurial unexpected development in Africa, exploring how the continent navigates systemic growth bottlenecks to position itself for the first time as a global frontier for digital innovation. The research identifies three core pillars of an enabling ecosystem that are regulations, infrastructure, and skills and analyzes their interplay in transforming resource constraints into opportunities for exponential development. Despite significant successes in markets like Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa, the study highlights critical challenges, including regulatory fragmentation across the AfCFTA, energy deficits, and rising cybersecurity threats. To transition from isolated local victories to a sustained continental success, the study proposes a permanent shift from reactive to proactive governance. Key policy recommendations include the institutionalization of regional fintech sandboxes, the deployment of hybrid infrastructure (solar and satellite), and the deepening of diaspora partnerships to bridge human capital gaps that currently exists in Mother Africa.

title: The Avant-Garde and Dystopias: The Global Political Economy of Upcycling

detail.title: The Avant-Garde and Dystopias: The Global Political Economy of Upcycling

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no conflicts of interest to disclose.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human subjects were used in this study.
declarations.funderStatement: The author has no external funding or financial conflicts of interest to disclose.

detail.abstract: This study examines the historical evolution of upcycling to explain how and why its function has shifted between political resistance and ecological practice over time. Rather than treating upcycling as a neutral or inherently sustainable activity, the analysis situates it within broader political and economic structures that shape material culture. Tracing its emergence, transformation, and contemporary circulation, the study demonstrates that upcycling is best understood as a politically contingent practice whose meanings and effects change with context. Methodologically, the study combines systematic content analysis, correlation analysis, and historical process tracing to capture both qualitative and quantitative dynamics. Sources include archival materials, avantgarde artworks, design objects, activist manifestos, media coverage, digital platform content, and policy documents spanning the twentieth and early twenty-first centuries. Content analysis identifies recurring themes and discursive frames associated with upcycling, while correlation analysis examines temporal relationships between economic downturns, political crises, and spikes in upcycling-related cultural production. Historical process tracing is used to link these patterns to shifts in political economy, industrial organization, and cultural institutions. The findings show that upcycling initially emerged within avant-garde and countercultural art movements as a deliberate critique of industrial capitalism. Early practitioners used discarded materials to expose the excesses of mass production, the invisibility of waste streams, and the ecological exploitation embedded in modern consumer culture. In this phase, upcycling functioned as an oppositional practice: its aesthetic strategies and material choices were inseparable from anti-capitalist and anti-industrial politics. Waste was not merely reused but symbolically re-signified to challenge dominant values of novelty, efficiency, and profit. Over time, however, these oppositional aesthetics were progressively absorbed into luxury fashion, design, and mainstream consumer markets. What began as a critique of overproduction became a marketable signifier of creativity, authenticity, and environmental awareness. The study documents how brands and institutions selectively adopted the visual language of upcycling while stripping it of its critical force. Statistical analysis reveals a strong correlation between periods of economic crisis or political upheaval, such as recessions or moments of intensified environmental debate, and renewed interest in upcycling practices. Yet these moments of resurgence are frequently followed by rapid commodification, suggesting a cyclical pattern in which dissent is repeatedly recuperated by markets. In the contemporary period, digital platforms play a central role in this dynamic. Social media and online marketplaces dramatically increase the visibility and accessibility of upcycling, enabling grassroots participation and transnational exchange. At the same time, these platforms accelerate commercialization by rewarding visibility, branding, and scalability. As a result, political critique and market logic coexist uneasily, often within the same practices and objects. These results indicate that upcycling cannot be classified as either inherently radical or inherently recuperative. Its political and ecological significance depends less on the act of material reuse itself than on the power relations, institutional settings, and economic structures through which it circulates. Understanding upcycling in this way has broader implications for sustainability discourse: material practices do not escape politics, and ecological interventions are always shaped by the conditions of their production, circulation, and consumption.

title: Analysis of Nigeria's 2026 Tax Regime: Anticipated Impact on SMEs and Low-Income Households

detail.title: Analysis of Nigeria's 2026 Tax Regime: Anticipated Impact on SMEs and Low-Income Households

declarations.ethicsApproval: The author utilized Large Language Models for the purpose of linguistic refinement, structural optimization, and the generation of standardized academic metadata. The core research, policy analysis, and data interpretation remain the original work of the author."

detail.abstract: The introduction of Nigeria's new consolidated tax regime, slated for January 1, 2026, represents a profound policy shift, aims to enhancing fiscal sustainability, improve compliance, and significantly increase the nation's tax-to-GDP ratio. This article analyzes the paradoxical dual-impact of these comprehensive reforms on two critical segments: Small and Medium Scale Enterprises (SMEs), the crucial engine of job creation and low-income households, the nation's most vulnerable demographic. On the positive side, the reforms establish a fairer system by offering generous Corporate Income Tax (CIT) exemption thresholds (₦100 million turnover) for microenterprises and specific Personal Income Tax (PIT) relief (₦800,000 annual income) for the working poor. Conversely, two major friction points threaten the intended social equity gains. First, the systemic push for digital compliance under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act (NTAA) imposes a disproportionate financial and technical burden on the vast, low-margin informal sector, risking involuntary non-compliance and operational resistance. Second, the progressive relief offered by the PIT exemption is immediately threatened by the regressive nature of indirect taxes and resultant cost-push inflation driven by tax base expansion, which severely and disproportionately impacts the purchasing power of the poor. The study concludes that the success of the 2026 Tax Regime hinges on curbing these inherent social costs. Strategic policy recommendations emphasize the legislative zero-rating of VAT on essential, poverty-line-anchored goods to create an "impenetrable fiscal shield"; integrating the informal sector through protection measures; the implementation of a phased and incentive-based digital compliance program for SMEs; establishing fair dispute resolution mechanisms and enforcing mandatory revenue transparency to build public trust and voluntary compliance.

title: Working Paper: The Effects of ESG Factors on Corporate Profitability

detail.title: Working Paper: The Effects of ESG Factors on Corporate Profitability
detail.abstract: The paper deals with the effects of ESG performance on corporate profitability among firms operating in developed European countries. The study seeks to determine whether and how the adoption of strong ESG practices influences financial outcomes, accounting for sectoral differences, firm size, and other firm-specific characteristics. The results confirm a predominantly positive effect of ESG performance and its individual components on the profitability of European companies over the period 2009–2024.

title: Maintenance Engineering Frameworks for Improving Emergency Preparedness and Operational Continuity in Africa

detail.title: Maintenance Engineering Frameworks for Improving Emergency Preparedness and Operational Continuity in Africa
detail.abstract: Emergency disruptions continue to undermine the reliability of critical infrastructure systems across Africa, exposing systemic weaknesses in maintenance practices and preparedness planning. This study examines how maintenance engineering frameworks can be strategically leveraged to improve emergency preparedness and operational continuity across African infrastructure systems. Using a systematic qualitative synthesis of existing literature, the study integrates concepts from preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance with business continuity and resilience management perspectives. The findings reveal that maintenance engineering is not merely a technical support function but a central determinant of preparedness, response effectiveness, and recovery speed during emergencies. Contrary to dominant assumptions, organizational culture and governance structures were found to be as influential as advanced technologies in determining maintenance readiness. The study concludes that integrated, context-sensitive maintenance engineering frameworks significantly enhance emergency preparedness and operational continuity in African settings. The paper contributes a structured framework tailored to resource-constrained environments and proposes actionable pathways for policymakers, infrastructure managers, and maintenance professionals seeking to strengthen resilience across critical sectors in Africa.

title: Systematic Approaches to Maintenance Optimization for Energy Security and Industrial Sustainability in Africa

detail.title: Systematic Approaches to Maintenance Optimization for Energy Security and Industrial Sustainability in Africa
detail.abstract: Energy security and industrial sustainability remain persistent challenges across African economies due to aging infrastructure, fragmented maintenance practices, and limited integration of emerging technologies. This study systematically examines maintenance optimization approaches that support reliable energy delivery and sustainable industrial performance in Africa. Drawing on peer-reviewed literature from energy systems, industrial engineering, and sustainability management, the study synthesizes preventive, predictive, corrective, and data-driven maintenance strategies. The findings indicate that integrated maintenance frameworks, particularly those combining Lean Six Sigma principles, reliability engineering, and artificial intelligence offer measurable improvements in asset availability, cost efficiency, and operational resilience. The study further reveals that maintenance optimization plays a structural role in energy security, extending beyond technical efficiency to institutional capacity, policy alignment, and long-term sustainability. Despite growing technological adoption, gaps remain in contextual adaptation, workforce readiness, and cross-sector coordination. The study concludes that systematic maintenance optimization is not merely a support function but a strategic enabler of Africa's energy security and industrial transformation. Future research should prioritize empirically grounded, Africa-specific maintenance models that align digital innovation with socio-technical realities.

title: Managing Complex Industrial Assets in Africa: Linking Maintenance Optimization, Reliability, and Human Performance

detail.title: Managing Complex Industrial Assets in Africa: Linking Maintenance Optimization, Reliability, and Human Performance
detail.abstract: Managing complex industrial assets in Africa has become increasingly challenging due to aging infrastructure, operational uncertainty, limited resources, and growing performance expectations across asset-intensive sectors such as energy, manufacturing, mining, and aviation. This study examines how maintenance optimization, reliability engineering, and human performance interact in shaping asset outcomes within African industrial contexts. A qualitative synthesis of existing scholarly literature was conducted to identify dominant maintenance strategies, reliability enhancement models, and human-centered asset management approaches relevant to African operations. The findings indicate that while maintenance optimization frameworks such as Lean Six Sigma and predictive maintenance have improved operational efficiency, their effectiveness remains constrained when human performance and organizational factors are insufficiently integrated. The study further reveals that reliability failures in African industrial systems are often socio-technical rather than purely technical in nature. The main conclusion of this research is that sustainable management of complex industrial assets in Africa requires an integrated framework that aligns maintenance optimization techniques with reliability objectives and human performance capabilities. This paper contributes to asset management scholarship by explicitly linking these three dimensions and contextualizing them within African industrial realities, thereby offering direction for both future research and practical implementation. title: From Offshore Platforms to Airports: Unified Maintenance Strategies for High-Risk African Infrastructure

detail.title: From Offshore Platforms to Airports: Unified Maintenance Strategies for High-Risk African Infrastructure
detail.abstract: High-risk infrastructure systems such as offshore oil platforms and airports play a critical role in Africa's economic stability, safety, and regional integration, yet they continue to experience recurrent failures linked to fragmented and reactive maintenance practices. This study examines maintenance strategies across offshore, aviation, marine, and energy infrastructure sectors in Africa with the aim of identifying transferable principles that support a unified maintenance framework. Using a systematic qualitative synthesis of peer-reviewed studies, policy reports, and sector-specific case analyses, the research evaluates predictive, preventive, corrective, and emergency-driven maintenance approaches. The findings reveal strong convergence in failure modes, human-factor vulnerabilities, and asset degradation patterns across sectors, despite differences in operational contexts. An unexpected outcome of the analysis is the demonstrated applicability of aviation emergency-response-centered maintenance logic to offshore and marine environments, where it improves readiness and resilience. The study concludes that unified maintenance strategies grounded in risk-based planning, human factors integration, and digital monitoring offer a more effective and context-sensitive solution for African high-risk infrastructure than sector-isolated models. The paper contributes a conceptual foundation for harmonized maintenance governance and offers practical implications for infrastructure operators and policymakers across the continent.

title: Socio-Technical Perspectives on Maintenance Optimization in African Energy and Manufacturing Sectors

detail.title: Socio-Technical Perspectives on Maintenance Optimization in African Energy and Manufacturing Sectors
detail.abstract: Maintenance optimization in African energy and manufacturing sectors remains a pressing challenge due to persistent inefficiencies, system downtime, and underutilized technical tools. This study applies a socio-technical perspective to understand how technical, organizational, human, and institutional factors jointly influence maintenance performance. Using a qualitative integrative approach based on literature from energy, manufacturing, and infrastructure-intensive industries across Africa, this study synthesizes findings from Lean Six Sigma frameworks, predictive and preventive maintenance models, and human factors studies. Key results indicate that maintenance optimization outcomes depend not only on the application of technical methodologies but also on workforce readiness, organizational culture, and governance structures. Notably, high-tech predictive systems underperform when socio-organizational alignment is weak, whereas adaptive practices in low-technology environments sometimes enhance resilience. The findings suggest that achieving sustainable maintenance optimization requires a shift from purely engineering-centric approaches toward integrated socio-technical frameworks that balance human, technical, and institutional factors. These insights have implications for policymakers, industry leaders, and practitioners seeking to improve reliability, sustainability, and efficiency in African energy and manufacturing sectors (Uke 2021; Nkosi 2020; Chatterjee and Rao 2020; Kirkegaard et al. 2023; Bowen 2025).

title: Asset Life Extension and Energy Reliability Through Integrated Maintenance Systems in African Industries

detail.title: Asset Life Extension and Energy Reliability Through Integrated Maintenance Systems in African Industries
detail.abstract: Asset degradation and unreliable energy supply remain persistent challenges across African industrial sectors, largely due to fragmented maintenance practices and aging infrastructure (Uke; Moshoma). This study investigates how integrated maintenance systems contribute to asset life extension and improved energy reliability in African industries. Using a systematic qualitative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature and documented industrial case studies, the research examines the combined application of predictive, preventive, corrective, and condition-based maintenance strategies (Ayu and Yunusa-Kaltungo; Wakiru et al.). The findings indicate that integrated maintenance systems significantly enhance asset longevity, reduce unplanned downtime, and stabilize energy output, particularly when supported by data analytics and real-time monitoring technologies (Adebisi et al.; Erhueh et al., "IoT"). Unexpectedly, organizational coordination and maintenance governance emerged as stronger reliability drivers than advanced technology alone (Mkandawire et al.; Paul et al.). The study concludes that integrated maintenance systems are not merely technical solutions but strategic enablers of sustainable energy reliability in African industries. The paper recommends context-sensitive maintenance integration frameworks and calls for future empirical validation within specific industrial sectors (Uke 2021; Fontana et al.).

title: Maintenance Optimization as a Catalyst for Industrial Safety, Reliability, and Sustainability in Africa

detail.title: Maintenance Optimization as a Catalyst for Industrial Safety, Reliability, and Sustainability in Africa
detail.abstract: Industrial safety, reliability, and sustainability are critical challenges in African manufacturing, energy, and aviation sectors. This study investigates how maintenance optimization can serve as a catalyst for addressing these challenges by integrating predictive, preventive, and corrective strategies. Using a comprehensive review of empirical studies, industrial reports, and case studies, this research identifies current gaps in African industrial maintenance practices. The findings demonstrate that optimized maintenance significantly reduces unplanned downtime, enhances equipment reliability, improves safety outcomes, and contributes to sustainable operations. Despite the challenges of technological adoption and workforce limitations, integrating advanced maintenance strategies provides measurable benefits for industries across Africa. Strategic recommendations include the adoption of predictive maintenance, workforce upskilling, and risk-based frameworks to maximize operational efficiency. These insights underscore maintenance optimization as a key driver for industrial growth, safety, and sustainability on the continent.

title: White Paper: RevelationPM 4-3-3 Hybrid Architecture™ with Simulator: Why AI-Accelerated Projects Demand a Unified Hybrid Architecture

detail.title: White Paper: RevelationPM 4-3-3 Hybrid Architecture™ with Simulator: Why AI-Accelerated Projects Demand a Unified Hybrid Architecture
detail.abstract: For twenty years, the project management industry has suffered from a "False Choice" between Predictive (Waterfall) and Agile methodologies. This binary approach is failing in the era of AI, leading organizations to produce "Watermelon Projects"-green on the outside (hitting milestones) but red on the inside (technical debt and burnout). This paper introduces the RevelationPM 4-3-3 Hybrid Architecture™, a unified operating system that integrates the stability of systems engineering with the adaptability of product discovery. We define the operational mechanics of Hybrid through the Fixed Core vs. Flexible Perimeter™ model and introduce the PAAD Protocol™ for integrating AI as a competent Co-Pilot. This architecture resolves the friction between compliance-heavy industries and the need for rapid digital adaptation.

title: The Governance-Integrated Monitoring Model (GIMM): Architecting Predictive AI Compliance Intelligence for Donor-Funded NGOs

detail.title: The Governance-Integrated Monitoring Model (GIMM): Architecting Predictive AI Compliance Intelligence for Donor-Funded NGOs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal, financial or professional conflict of interest in relation to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on conceptual modelling, secondary literature and anonymized institutional practice insights. formal ethics committee approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: Donor-funded non-governmental organizations (NGOs) continue to experience persistent financial non-compliance, procurement violations, grant leakage and delayed fraud detection. These challenges are largely rooted in audit-centric governance models that remain retrospective and fragmented. This study introduces the Governance-Integrated Monitoring Model (GIMM) a governance-integrated RegTech architecture that embeds predictive artificial intelligence into NGO financial ecosystems to enable continuous, real-time and forward-looking compliance assurance. Using a design science research approach, GIMM is developed as a scalable public financial governance model integrating donor regulations, procurement thresholds, budgetary controls and ethical governance principles into a unified predictive compliance intelligence layer. The model reframes NGO accountability by replacing periodic audit assurance with continuous predictive governance intelligence.

title: Data-Driven and Human-Centered Maintenance Models for Sustainable Industrial Development in Africa

detail.title: Data-Driven and Human-Centered Maintenance Models for Sustainable Industrial Development in Africa
detail.abstract: Industrial development in Africa is constrained by inefficient maintenance practices, aging infrastructure, and limited adoption of advanced technologies. This study explores the integration of data-driven maintenance models with human-centered approaches to improve sustainability, resilience, and operational efficiency across African industries. A mixed-method approach, combining historical maintenance data, interviews with engineers and managers, and case study analysis, was employed. Key findings reveal that predictive analytics significantly reduces downtime while human-centered interventions enhance decision-making, safety, and maintenance compliance. The integration of these approaches creates sustainable industrial frameworks that extend asset lifespans and improve overall productivity. The study concludes that harmonizing technological efficiency with human-centered processes is critical for sustainable industrial development in Africa, highlighting practical implications for policymakers and industry managers.

title: Corporate Credit Risk Under Misaligned Transition Expectations: A Firm-Level Modeling Approach

detail.title: Corporate Credit Risk Under Misaligned Transition Expectations: A Firm-Level Modeling Approach
detail.abstract: Climate transition stress tests typically rely on exogenously imposed transition scenarios, implicitly assuming that firms perfectly anticipate future policies, technologies and market conditions. In practice, however, corporate decision-making under transition uncertainty crucially depends on firms' own expectations, which may be misaligned with the realized transition pathway and significantly affect their financial resilience. This paper develops a firm-level credit risk model to assess how misaligned transition expectations shape corporate default risk. Extending the framework of [Ndiaye et al., 2024a], we allow firms to form imperfect anticipations and to re-evaluate their strategies as the transition unfolds. Using a stochastic representation of sales, carbon intensity and production costs, combined with nested Monte Carlo simulations, we quantify how misanticipating carbon prices, abatement costs or demand-side adjustments affects probabilities of default. Numerical illustrations on fictitious firms show that pessimistic anticipations may reduce default risk by inducing early adjustments, whereas overly optimistic expectations can sharply increase default probabilities, particularly for carbon-intensive firms. Overall, our results highlight that transition risk cannot be fully captured by carbon-price shocks alone and that expectation formation constitutes a key, yet overlooked, transmission channel of climate transition risk in corporate credit portfolios.

title: Impact of Organisational Justice on Employees’ Burnout and Workplace Cynicism in DHL International Ltd in South-West, Nigeria

detail.title: Impact of Organisational Justice on Employees’ Burnout and Workplace Cynicism in DHL International Ltd in South-West, Nigeria
detail.abstract: This study investigated how distributive, procedural and interactional justice are practiced in DHL International Ltd in SouthWest Nigeria and examined their combined and relative effects on employees' burnout and workplace cynicism. Using data from 212 employees selected through stratified sampling across six states, the study assessed burnout dimensions (emotional exhaustion, depersonalisation and personal accomplishment) and cynicism components (cognitive, affective and behavioural) through standardised questionnaires. Descriptive and inferential analyses, including regression, correlation, t-tests and chisquare, showed that organisational justice strongly predicted burnout (R = .895) and workplace cynicism (R = .635). Higher justice perceptions were associated with reduced burnout and lower levels of cynicism, with procedural-interactional justice emerging most influential. The study concludes that fairness in organisational processes and interpersonal treatment plays a crucial role in reducing negative employee outcomes and enhancing organisational effectiveness. It recommends that organisations embed justice principles to minimise burnout and cynicism, and highlights the broader applicability of the findings for private-sector management practice.

title: A Fuzzy Decision Support Model for Selecting and Prioritising Improvement Initiatives in the Context of Operational Excellence: Application to a Mining Company
affiliations: Mohammadia School of Engineering, The School of Textile and Clothing industries (ESITH)  and Rabat National School of Mines

detail.title: A Fuzzy Decision Support Model for Selecting and Prioritising Improvement Initiatives in the Context of Operational Excellence: Application to a Mining Company
detail.abstract: In today's industrial environment, companies are constantly seeking to improve their operational performance and strengthen their competitiveness. However, selecting and prioritising improvement initiatives remains a complex task for decision-makers. Indeed, the diversity of criteria to be taken into account, combined with the multiplicity of actors involved and the subjectivity of their judgements, makes the process particularly delicate. Thus, this process falls squarely within the category of multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) problems.This article proposes a decision support model based on fuzzy logic, designed to help companies select and prioritise their improvement initiatives. The model evaluates each initiative using an overall relevance score calculated on the basis of five input indicators: efficiency, feasibility, cost, implementation time and originality. The applicability of the approach is illustrated through a case study conducted within a mining company. The results obtained were compared with those from the method currently used by the company in order to assess the consistency and relevance of the proposed fuzzy model in relation to existing practices.The results confirm the relevance of using fuzzy logic for selecting and prioritising improvement initiatives. The model developed makes it possible to better manage the uncertainty and subjectivity inherent in managerial decisions. It is therefore an effective and flexible decision-making tool that can support companies in their continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.

title: Toward a Holistic Maintenance Engineering Framework for African Industrial and Energy Systems

detail.title: Toward a Holistic Maintenance Engineering Framework for African Industrial and Energy Systems
detail.abstract: Maintenance engineering is crucial for sustaining industrial and energy operations, yet African systems face fragmented practices, technological gaps, and workforce challenges. This study examines existing maintenance strategies, human factors, and reliability frameworks across African industrial and energy sectors to propose a holistic maintenance engineering framework. Through a systematic literature review, integration of predictive, preventive, and corrective maintenance approaches, and analysis of workforce readiness and digital tools, critical gaps were identified. Findings indicate that while digital twins and predictive maintenance improve system reliability, human factor readiness remains a significant barrier. The proposed framework integrates maintenance methodologies, reliability modeling, and workforce considerations to optimize industrial and energy operations. Adoption of this framework can enhance operational efficiency, reduce downtime, and extend asset lifecycles, providing a structured path for sustainable industrialization across African nations (Uke, 2021; Ayu & Yunusa-Kaltungo, 2020; Okuh et al., 2025).

title: Sustainable Housing Delivery and Urban Regeneration in Dundee, Scotland: Planning Policy, Practice, and Implications for Medium-Sized Cities

detail.title: Sustainable Housing Delivery and Urban Regeneration in Dundee, Scotland: Planning Policy, Practice, and Implications for Medium-Sized Cities
